rules.statement: Compare token hash claims (at_hash, c_hash, s_hash) and similar secret-derived values with CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals, never with string equality.
rules.why: A constant-time comparison avoids leaking how much of the expected value matched through timing.
rules.check: Look for ==, string.Equals or SequenceEqual used to compare a computed hash or secret against a claim or input.

rules.statement: Get the hash for at_hash, c_hash and s_hash from the signature algorithm's defined token hash function, not from the digest size in the alg name.
rules.why: The alg suffix gives the wrong digest for Ed25519 (SHA-512) and Ed448 (SHAKE256, 114 bytes).
rules.check: Look for code that parses the alg suffix (256/384/512) or maps alg names to SHA-2 functions to compute token hashes.

rules.statement: Compute and verify left-most-half token hashes in one shared helper used by both issuer and validator, not in separate implementations.
rules.why: If the server and client share one implementation, they encode the hash the same way.
rules.check: Look for a new hand-written left-half/base64url hash computation instead of a call to the shared helper.

rules.statement: Compute token hashes over the value's ASCII octets: verification returns false for a non-ASCII value or claim, and computation throws ArgumentException for a non-ASCII value.
rules.why: OIDC Core §3.1.3.6 defines the hash over the ASCII octets.
rules.check: Look for UTF-8 encoding of the hashed value with no ASCII check, or for non-ASCII input being accepted silently.

rules.statement: Validate an ID token under an asymmetric-only algorithm policy that never permits symmetric algorithms or `none`, intersected with the client's configured and provider-advertised algorithms, and fail validation when the intersection is empty.
rules.why: A symmetric or unsecured ID token must never be accepted, whatever the provider advertises.
rules.check: Look for ID-token validation that allows HS*, `none`, or the provider's advertised list without filtering, or that falls back to all algorithms when the intersection is empty.

rules.statement: Pass the permitted algorithms to the JWT validator as its valid signature algorithms, so the header alg is checked before any cryptographic operation.
rules.why: Rejecting a disallowed alg early stops the token from steering which cryptography runs.
rules.check: Look for alg checks done after signature verification, or validation with no explicit list of allowed algorithms.

rules.statement: Configure an OAuth/OIDC client's per-registration settings (such as allowed ID-token signing algorithms) on the client registration, not as process-wide configuration.
rules.why: Two clients in one process can register different values with their providers.
rules.check: Look for per-client protocol settings added to global options or static configuration.

rules.statement: Validate an algorithm-list option in its setter: reject blank entries, `none` and duplicates.
rules.why: An invalid list should fail when it is configured, not at validation time.
rules.check: Look for algorithm-list properties whose setter or init accessor stores input without checking it.

rules.statement: When a JWT header names a kid the cached key set lacks, refresh the key set once (rate-limited by the cache) and fail validation if the key is still missing.
rules.why: This handles key rotation without letting attacker-chosen kids cause unbounded fetches.
rules.check: Look for repeated or unthrottled JWKS refreshes on unknown kid, or for falling back to an arbitrary key when the kid is not found.

rules.statement: Check ID-token claims per OIDC Core: iss equals the discovered issuer, aud contains the client id, exp and iat are required, typ if present is `JWT`, sub is non-empty, azp if present equals the client id, nonce matches ordinally, and auth_time satisfies max_age with the clock skew.
rules.why: OIDC Core §3.1.3.7 requires these checks, and the typ check rejects other JWT types such as logout+jwt and at+jwt.
rules.check: Look for ID-token validation that skips any of these checks, uses culture-sensitive or case-insensitive comparison, or accepts other typ values.

rules.statement: In the authorization code flow, accept an absent at_hash/c_hash/s_hash, but require a present one to be a string that verifies against the value the request supplies.
rules.why: These claims are optional in the code flow, so requiring them would reject valid tokens from conforming providers.
rules.check: Look for code that rejects tokens missing these claims, or that skips verifying a claim that is present.

rules.statement: Return an invalid token as a validation result with a failure reason, but still throw for infrastructure failures and cancellation, rethrowing them when an inner validator has caught them.
rules.why: Callers need the token outcome as a value, while provider failures and cancellation must not be hidden as invalid-token results.
rules.check: Look for validators that throw on a bad token, or that turn OperationCanceledException or provider exceptions caught by an inner component into a failed result.

rules.statement: Never put token text in failure reasons or messages; map exceptions whose message embeds the token to a fixed message.
rules.why: JwtDecodeException messages contain the whole token, which would leak a credential.
rules.check: Look for exception messages from JWT decoding or key lookup copied into results, logs or responses.

rules.statement: Use a caller-supplied stack buffer sized to the hash output for hash computation and comparison, so verification does not allocate on the heap.
rules.why: Several hash checks can share one stack buffer, and the comparison makes no heap allocation.
rules.check: Look for byte[] allocations or ToArray calls in hash compute or verify paths where a stackalloc'd span would do.
